title: Make the order dispatcher's futures say what happened

blocks.text: The returns service archives incoming orders on a small worker pool. Its support queue has three complaints this week: a customer who submitted the same return twice has two archive entries; an order hit a moment when the archive volume was busy and was never archived, although the dispatcher is meant to retry such failures; and an order the archive refused every time was reported as archived.

`OrderDispatch.dispatch(...)` already decides what to archive, retries and reports. It reads only the `Future`s that two methods return, and those two are still `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/OrderDispatch.java`:

items: `remember(orderId)`: records the id on the pool; `dispatch` skips the order when the `Future`'s value is `false`;

`store(orderId)`: stores the order with `archive.store(...)` on the pool; `dispatch` retries when the `Future` fails with an `IOException` as its cause, and treats a `Future` that ends normally as stored.

blocks.text: Keep the signatures: other callers depend on `Future<?>`. About four lines in total.
The tests run the dispatcher on a real `ExecutorService` with an archive that refuses some stores.

cases.says: with a healthy archive, every distinct order is stored once, by a pool thread, and reported as archived
an order id that comes again is not stored again: the Future of remember() tells a new id from a repeat
an archive failure reaches dispatch() with the archive's IOException as the cause, so it is retried and the order is stored
an order the archive never takes is reported as failed, not as archived

origin.section: When a Body Fits Both, the Overload That Returns a Value Wins

concepts: When a body fits both a void and a value-returning interface and its parameter types are known, the value-returning overload is chosen, so braces or a return decide what submit's Future holds and whether a checked exception reaches it.
